ev.q: During June–October 2023, five cases of neonatal enterovirus infection were identified at Rady Children’s Hospital in San Diego, California.
Four infants had thrombocytopenia, and three had hepatitis with coagulopathy. Serum ferritin levels were elevated in three neonates.
Four of the five patients’ plasma also tested positive for enterovirus by reverse transcription−polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).
Coxsackie B5 was identified in three specimens and Coxsackie B4 in one.
Pertinent laboratory values* and clinical features of neonatal patients with enterovirus infection

public_health_question.v: What were the clinical features and viral types in a cluster of neonatal enterovirus infections, and can respiratory virus panel PCR aid early diagnosis?

ev.q: Respiratory panel polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing for rhinovirus-enterovirus facilitated diagnosis of enterovirus infection in these infants.
Respiratory Viral Panel as an Early Diagnostic Tool for Neonatal Enterovirus Infection
subsequently identified as Coxsackie B4 and B5 infections, occurred in San Diego, California.
Mothers of three of the infants received a diagnosis of chorioamnionitis before delivery

equity.level_reason: Only age (neonates) defines the population and sex is listed per patient; no social-position dimension is analyzed or framed.

notes: Five-patient descriptive case series; lab values judged against reference ranges are clinical classification, not comparisons. Serotype percentages (82.7%, 16.7%) are cited from a prior review. Called a cluster, but no outbreak investigation methods are described, so case report/series was chosen.
